features.feature: Stream lines (every river, creek and stream)
features.how: Geometry, names and stream order as published; simplified to about 20 m.

features.feature: Stream names and 'also called' names
features.how: OFFICIAL_NM and COMMON_NM.

features.feature: Stream size filter (Strahler order)
features.how: STR_ORDER.

features.feature: Watershed (HUC) and FWMIS ID in details
features.how: HUC_8 and WB_ID.

features.feature: Species on each stretch of stream (colour and code labels)
features.how: Survey records whose location is within 0.5 km of that stream reach, on the same waterbody ID (FWMIS) or same name inside the park (Parks Canada).

features.feature: Survey site dots and their species, years and methods
features.how: Record locations as published; sites that do not lie on a mapped water are shown on their own.

features.feature: Species years (e.g. 1985-2020) and the 'Records from' filter
features.how: Survey dates (Waterton lakes: 2011 'present' column).

features.feature: 'FWMIS list for the whole river system' in stream details
features.how: SPECIES_PRES, shown for reference only; not used to colour streams.

features.feature: Lake outlines and names
features.how: Geometry and names as published.

features.feature: Species recorded in each lake
features.how: Lake SPECIES_PRES plus survey records in the lake; Waterton lakes matched by name inside the park.

features.feature: Stocking records and 'stocked' badge
features.how: Stocking species and years joined by waterbody ID.

features.feature: Species names for the four-letter codes
features.how: SPEC_CODE / SPEC_NAME pairs from the FWMIS survey layer; Parks Canada codes mapped with their data dictionaries (RBTR = RNTR, BRTR = BNTR, BUBT = BURB, PYWH = PGWH, CTTR/RBTR hybrid = CRTR).

features.feature: Banff watershed note (Cascade, Panther, Spray)
features.how: Species with sites occupied in either replicate.

features.feature: Park records with no map location
features.how: Records that could not be matched to a mapped water by name and location.

features.feature: Species colours, rarity order for colouring, legend layout
features.how: Display choices made for this map; not data.

features.feature: Basemaps and overlays
features.how: Map tiles loaded from each provider.

features.feature: Route planner auto-routing and "Route here from me"
features.how: OSRM car, bike or foot profile; straight lines when offline. Start point from your device location.

features.feature: Route distance and time
features.how: Distance calculated in the app from the route line; travel time is the routing service estimate.

features.feature: My location
features.how: Your device's GPS through the browser.

features.feature: Regulation links
features.how: Links only.

features.feature: Trail names and trail lines (zoom 13+)
features.how: Paths, footways, tracks and bridleways that have a name, an operator, or belong to a hiking route in OpenStreetMap. A trail with no name of its own takes its hiking route's name, or '<operator> trail'. Trails with an operator, route or ref are drawn darker as official. Nothing is labelled that OSM does not name.

features.feature: Towns, villages, hamlets (zoom 8+), peaks, hills, passes, ridges, glaciers, waterfalls, campsites, huts, trailheads, viewpoints and historic sites (zoom 10+)
features.how: Named OSM nodes only, with elevation where OSM gives it. Settlements and higher summits are labelled first when space is short.

features.feature: Place-name overlay
features.how: Esri reference label tiles drawn above the faded basemap.

features.feature: Species filter groups (game fish vs non-game species)
features.how: Codes from FWMIS whose species is on Schedule 1 Part 1 (Arctic grayling, goldeye, lake sturgeon, mooneye, sauger, tullibee/cisco, plus the trout, whitefish, pike, walleye, perch and burbot already listed) are game fish. All other codes go in the Non-game species group; amphibian, mollusc, crayfish and family-level or unknown records are listed separately inside it. Hybrids and kokanee keep the groups in data/species.json.

features.feature: Route line types (paved road, gravel or dirt road, road with surface not mapped, on foot)
features.how: OSRM returns the OpenStreetMap nodes the route passes; each stretch takes the highway, surface and tracktype tags of the OSM way that holds it. Paths, footways, bridleways and steps are 'on foot'. Roads with no surface tag are shown as 'surface not mapped' rather than guessed.

features.feature: Parking areas and 'on foot from here' points on routes
features.how: Public parking areas (amenity=parking, not private) from OSM near where the route leaves a road and at the route ends. 'Drive, then hike' drives to the mapped parking area within 10 km of the destination that gives the shortest walk; if none is mapped, the drive ends where the road comes closest.

features.feature: Road names (zoom 12+; streets and service roads from zoom 14)
features.how: OSM roads with a name tag (e.g. Range Road 53, Township Road 82, Coal Camp Road) or a route number; numbered highways without a name show as 'Hwy <number>'. Roads with neither are not labelled.

features.feature: Species codes on hover
features.how: Hovering (or tapping) a stream stretch or lake shows its name and the selected species recorded there. 'Always show species code labels' brings back the permanent labels.
